### Observed differences

- In the later window, a previously unobserved activity A02 appears at the very end of traces: it was not observed in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) and afterwards occurs in about 57 in 100 traces, always as the final event (mean and median position 1.0, no spread). [OCC002, POS002]
- Activities that previously ended traces now lead into A02: A16 and A19 were observed only as the last event before (mean position 1.0), afterwards their mean positions are about 0.85 and every observed outgoing transition of each goes to A02 (30 and 44 transitions); A09 also now leads to A02 in about half of its outgoing transitions, where before it split between A13 (48%) and A14 (52%). [POS007, POS008, DIR006, DIR008, DIR004]
- A second new activity A01 appears in about 15 in 100 traces (0 before), late in the trace (mean position about 0.71); it is always followed by A16 and always precedes A02 when both occur, so roughly 15 in 100 traces now run A01 → A16 → A02. Correspondingly, A17 and A10, which previously routed to A16, now route to A01 in about half of their outgoing transitions (A17: 69% A15 / 31% A16 before, 50% A01 / 50% A15 after; A10: 48% A15 / 52% A16 before, 58% A15 / 42% A01 after). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL009, DIR007, DIR005]
- A02 now runs together with activities that previously appeared without it: with A14 together in 39 in 100 traces after (before never together, A14 alone in 37 in 100), with A03 in 35 in 100 (before A03 alone in 30 in 100), and similarly for A07, A09, A19, A13 and A10, with the partner typically running before A02. [REL008, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL010, REL007, REL006]
- Other differences: A14 now runs earlier (mean position about 0.39 → 0.20) at similar participation (about 37–39 in 100 traces); A09 occurs less often and later (mean occurrences 1.07 → 0.38, participation 37 → 20 in 100, mean position about 0.26 → 0.59); A13 occurs much less often and later (participation 23 → 9 in 100); A07 now leads to A14 instead of A09, and A03 now sometimes leads to A09 (about 19% of its outgoing transitions) while A08 drops from about 19% to 3%; pairs that often ran together before now mostly run separately (A09–A14 together 37 → 13 in 100, A13–A14 23 → 4 in 100, A09–A19 22 → 0), and several pairwise step distances shifted, some on small support. [OCC003, POS003, OCC004, POS005, POS006, DIR003, DIR002, REL011, REL013, REL012, LAG002, LAG007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a new closing stage was appended to the process in the later window: traces end with the previously unobserved activity A02 (about 57 in 100 traces, always last), into which the formerly terminal activities A16 and A19 now flow, and A09 now flows into A02 instead of A14; in about 15 in 100 traces a new activity A01 is inserted before A16, forming the chain A01 → A16 → A02, with A17 and A10 rerouted from A16 to A01 in roughly half of their outgoing transitions. [OCC002, POS002, DIR006, DIR008, DIR004, OCC001, DIR001, REL001, REL002, DIR007, DIR005]

The placement is shown directly rather than inferred: successor evidence shows A16, A19 and A09 leading into A02 and A01 leading to A16 in essentially all observed transitions; position evidence shows A02 at the trace end and A16/A19 moving from the end to about position 0.85; relation evidence shows A02 co-occurring with seven activities that previously ran without it, always after them. The picture is consistent across occurrence, position, direction and relation indicators, though many items describe the same insertion and are not independent confirmations, and the after-window routing shares rest on moderate counts (about 30–76 outgoing transitions). An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is relabelling: zero participation in the earlier window only shows A02 and A01 were not observed, not that they are genuinely new rather than renamed activities. [POS007, POS008, DIR006, DIR004, REL008, REL003]

Other differences: A14 now runs earlier at similar participation, A13 and A09 occur less often and later, A07 now leads to A14 rather than A09, A03 sometimes leads to A09, and the frequent co-occurrence of A09–A14, A13–A14 and A09–A19 largely disappeared; these are consistent with a reordering around A14 and a reduced A09/A13 segment, but are reported separately from the main hypothesis. [POS006, OCC004, OCC003, DIR003, REL011, REL013, REL012]
